papers.title: A multi-method explainable AI for analyzing hybrid SARIMAX-GRU temperature forecasting in high-temperature data centers
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“AI × 气候”：标题或摘要命中 deep learning、explainable、shap、artificial intelligence、temperature，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: Introduction Accurate temperature prediction is essential for improving energy efficiency and ensuring reliable operation in modern data centers. However, despite their high accuracy, deep learning forecasting models often lack interpretability, limiting their deployment in critical environments. This study extends a previously developed hybrid SARIMAX-GRU forecasting model by introducing an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) framework to analyze and validate its decision-making process under different operating conditions. Methods The proposed framework employs four XAI techniques, including SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME), Integrated Gradients, and Permutation Importance, to analyze the contribution of temporal residual features in temperature prediction. The analysis considers nine scenarios covering low, moderate, and high temperatures (24 °C, 27 °C, and 30 °C) with workload transitions between 50%, 75%, and 100%. Pearson and Spearman correlation analyses are used to evaluate the agreement between explanation methods in terms of importance scores and feature rankings, respectively. Results The results show that the hybrid SARIMAX-GRU model mainly depends on recent residual features, particularly Residual_t1 to Residual_t4, while older residuals have limited influence. The dominant features vary according to workload transitions and sensor locations, reflecting changes in thermal dynamics. SHAP, Integrated Gradients, and Permutation Importance demonstrate highly consistent explanations, with Pearson correlations ranging from 0.93 to 1.00, while LIME provides more variable but complementary interpretations. Spearman correlation analysis further confirms strong agreement in feature rankings among SHAP, Integrated Gradients, and Permutation Importance, whereas rank agreement involving LIME varies across scenarios. Discussion The XAI analysis confirms that the model captures meaningful short-term thermal dependencies rather than arbitrary patterns. The variations in feature importance across different operating conditions highlight the model's ability to adapt to changing thermal behaviors, while the agreement among multiple XAI techniques improves confidence in the generated explanations. Conclusion This study demonstrates that integrating XAI with hybrid temperature forecasting enhances model transparency and provides valuable insights into data center thermal prediction. The proposed framework supports more trustworthy intelligent cooling and energy optimization decisions by identifying the key factors influencing model predictions.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Hourly Land–Atmosphere Interaction Dataset from a Coordinated 15-Station Network Spanning the Environmental Gradients of the Tibetan Plateau (2021–24)
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“青藏高原”：标题或摘要命中 tibetan plateau、plateau、atmospher、monsoon、temperature，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: Abstract Accurate characterization of land–atmosphere interactions over the Tibetan Plateau (TP) is hindered by fragmented measurements, inconsistent data-processing standards, and a scarcity of integrated, multi-component observations. To address these limitations, we present an integrated dataset from 15 stations spanning monsoon-dominated, westerlies-dominated, and transitional regions of the TP. The dataset features hourly gradient meteorological variables, radiation components, soil temperature and moisture measurements, and turbulent fluxes, providing vertically resolved information on land surface processes. Processed under standardized protocols with harmonized temporal resolutions, consistent variable definitions, and rigorous quality control procedures, the data ensure high reliability and internal consistency. This dataset provides a robust observational foundation for advancing process-based understanding of land–atmosphere coupling and its representation in models over the TP. It is expected to support land surface and Earth system model evaluation, satellite product validation, and data assimilation. Furthermore, it provides a basis for developing hybrid physics-machine learning approaches for data quality control and gap-filling in-situ observations in complex high-altitude environments.

papers.title: Detection and characterization of deep convective clouds over the Tibetan plateau and Asian Monsoon regions using hyperspectral infrared sounders
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“青藏高原”：标题或摘要命中 tibetan plateau、himalaya、plateau、ocean、monsoon，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: A novel method for detecting deep convective clouds based on the height of inverted hyperspectral infrared spectra near 9.6 μm, i.e., H-index, is presented. Verification to their cloud top heights using Single Field-of-View Retrieval Products (SiFSAP) and CERES products demonstrates that this method provide an effective way to detect the deep convective clouds, with the DCCs detected using H-index >3.5 K being mostly above 250 hPa, and DCCi2 detected by H-index >11.5 K mostly above 150 hPa. Further analysis of the spatiotemporal distribution of these two categories of DCCs and DCCi2 over the Tibetan Plateau (TP) and surrounding Asian Monsoon regions using 13 years of CrIS data (2013–2025) reveals: (1) Frequent DCCs occur over the Western Himalaya, Pakistan, Northwest India during summer, and western Himalayan DCCs are significantly more likely to intensify into DCCi2 compared to those over the TP, confirming previous findings of extreme deep convection along steep Himalayan slopes; (2) The occurrence of DCCs over the TP exhibits a strong correlation with ENSO cycles, with less DCCS during El Niño years (2015, 2019) and more DCCs during La Niña year (2022), and DCCs over the TP shows a decreasing trend: and (3) nighttime (∼1:30 am) DCCs are more frequent than daytime (∼1:30 pm) over the TP. Notably, frequent DCCs occurrence is found near Ya’an, Sichuan (the “Rain City”), particularly during summer nights. Frequent DCCs are also evident over the Bay of Bengal and South China Sea. From the annual cycle of DCCs, the maximum DCCs occurrence over the Western Himalaya and TP lags behind ocean regions by approximately 1 month, reflecting monsoon propagation dynamics. These results demonstrate the value of hyperspectral infrared data for studying DCCs over the TP and Asian Monsoon regions. This new method can be easily applied to other hyperspectral infrared sounders, such as AIRS and IASI, enabling DCC studies in other regions and facilitating climatological analysis using over 20 years of accumulated hyperspectral sounder data from AIRS, IASI and CrIS.

papers.title: Forest structural mediation of hydrological processes and ecosystem multifunctionality: mechanisms, trade-offs, and adaptive management
papers.journal: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“AI × 气候”：标题或摘要命中 machine learning、causal、climate、precipitation、hydrolog，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: Forests provide multiple ecosystem services, including water regulation, water supply, soil retention, carbon sequestration, habitat provision, biodiversity conservation, and timber production. These services arise from coupled processes operating across vegetation, litter, soil, and watershed compartments. Changes in climate, land use, forest structure, or management can therefore alter several services simultaneously, but the direction of change depends on the process pathway, environmental context, and scale of assessment. Here, we synthesize advances in the quantitative assessment of interactions between forest hydrological functions and other ecosystem services, emphasizing how environmental drivers and management reorganize forest structure, how structural states alter hydrological partitioning and water-carbon coupling, and how these process changes propagate to ecosystem-service outcomes. We first establish a process-based framework covering canopy interception, throughfall, stemflow, litter interception, infiltration, evapotranspiration, soil-water storage, deep drainage, groundwater recharge, lateral flow, baseflow, and surface runoff. We then evaluate field experiments, watershed observations, process-based and ecosystem-service models, spatial statistics, machine learning, and causal inference, with explicit attention to their assumptions and scale limitations. Quantitative evidence from global thinning syntheses and classical catchment experiments is used to distinguish relatively consistent responses from context-dependent ones. A long-term Korean pine forest-management experiment on Changbai Mountain is included as an illustrative case study: the treatments persisted for 27 years, whereas the hydrological measurements summarized here represent observations made in 2023 rather than a continuous 27-year hydrological time series. The case illustrates how post-treatment structural states are associated with differences in precipitation partitioning and soil-water processes, but it is not presented as a formal causal mediation test. We further identify knowledge gaps involving belowground hydraulic redistribution, nonlinear thresholds, temporal legacies, cross-scale interactions, causal attribution, and model uncertainty, and propose a research and management framework linking long-term experiments, remote sensing, process-based models, causal inference, and multi-objective optimization.

papers.title: Drought to Flood Abrupt Alternation Events Across Monsoon Region in China: Characteristics, Mechanisms, and Crop Exposure
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“东亚气候”：标题或摘要命中 monsoon、yangtze、precipitation、climate、circulation，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: Abstract Climate change is altering the frequency and intensity of hydroclimatic extremes, increasing the likelihood of drought to flood abrupt alternation (DTFAA) events which creates compound risks. Here, we identify DTFAA events across the monsoon region of China (MRC) during May–September from 1961 to 2023 using the daily Standardized Weighted Average Precipitation index. We identify 3,575 DTFAA events, with most transitions occurring within 1–2 days and a modest maximum in June. Generally, DTFAA frequency and intensity in MRC increase significantly at rates of 0.29 times decade⁻¹ and 0.26 decade⁻¹, respectively, with high frequencies concentrated in the middle and lower Yangtze River Basin, southern coastal China, and parts of North and Southwest China. Dynamically, governed by jet-waveguide interaction, the transition initiates with high-latitude easterly anomalies anchoring upstream blocking and the westward-extending subtropic high priming baroclinicity. Subsequently, the intensified and westward-extending subtropical jet establishes a mid-latitude meridional potential vorticity gradient conduit, routing trapped energy in blocking downstream to drive deep dynamic suction and moisture convergence, unleashing the abrupt flooding. Furthermore, crop exposure is crop-specific heterogeneous: maize and wheat show extensive high-exposure belts, whereas rice exposure is more fragmented; maize exhibits significant increases in both frequency and intensity exposure during 2000–2019. These results demonstrate that DTFAA events in the MRC arise from coordinated large-scale circulation and moisture-transport processes and that their agricultural consequences are strongly crop and region dependent, providing a dynamical and impact-oriented framework for improving monitoring, prediction, and adaptation to rapid hydroclimatic transitions.

papers.title: Monitoring Marine Microplastic Distributions in Data-Scarce Ocean Regions Using Environmental Representation Learning and Explainable Machine Learning
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“AI × 气候”：标题或摘要命中 machine learning、explainable、shap、ocean、temperature，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: Monitoring pollution in the ocean from microplastic and making decisions using this data is challenging, especially in ocean areas with little data and geographically limited observations. The ability to accurately predict microplastic distributions is crucial for the identification of pollution hotspots and for understanding environmental risk and for taking decisions on marine conservation. This study introduces a framework for learning a representation of the environment which is explainable and aware of uncertainty that combines NOAA marine microplastic observation data with oceanographic and geospatial data provided by Copernicus Marine and GEBCO datasets. The proposed Contrastive-XGBoost model outperformed the other models with the highest predictive capability with R2 = 0.651, RMSE = 1.008 and MAE = 0.619. Predictors identified by SHAP analysis included depth, bathymetry, geographical location, temperature, ocean circulation, and proximity to coast. Ablation analysis revealed the advantage of using combined (heterogeneous) environmental variables. Global prediction maps indicated that coastal and semi-enclosed seas, such as the Bay of Bengal, South China Sea, Gulf of Mexico and Mediterranean Sea are potentially accumulation hotspots. Conventional XGBoost, however, showed statistically comparable predictive power and geographically independent validation showed a limited transferability to environmentally different regions. The results show the possibility of using interpretable environmental machine learning for supplying additional data for environmental pollution monitoring, hotspot detection and uncertainty aware environmental decision-making.

papers.title: Enhanced Sensitivity of the Asian Water Tower to La Niña in the 21st Century
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“青藏高原”：标题或摘要命中 tibetan plateau、plateau、monsoon、precipitation、circulation，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: Abstract The Tibetan Plateau (TP) is a key water source for downstream Asia, and its rainy‐season precipitation is influenced by the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO). However, whether this teleconnection has remained stationary over recent decades remains uncertain. Using multi‐source data sets, we examine ENSO‐related precipitation, circulation, and moisture‐transport composites during the pre‐2000 epoch (1979–2000) and the post‐2001 epoch (2001–2023). ENSO lifecycle composites show that El Niño and La Niña are associated with opposite‐signed precipitation responses through changes in Western Pacific Subtropical High (WPSH) displacement and monsoon moisture transport. In the post‐2001 epoch, the sensitivity of the plateau's rainy‐season precipitation to La Niña is enhanced: La Niña‐related wetting and WPSH responses are larger in the composites, with a more westward‐displaced WPSH and enhanced moisture transport toward the plateau.

papers.title: Monsoon and Tropical Cyclones shape mid-latitude precipitation in East Asia during the early Eocene hothouse climate
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“东亚气候”：标题或摘要命中 east asia、monsoon、precipitation、climate、atmospher，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: Abstract The Asian mid-latitudes experienced a subtropical arid belt during most of the Eocene hothouse climate. This interpretation is supported by climate model simulations, but is in contrast with new proxy reconstructions, which indicate greening during the early Eocene. Here, we investigate the discrepancy between models and proxies by analysing the atmospheric circulation in the modelled climate. We assess the contribution of monsoonal circulation, extratropical and tropical cyclones to precipitation, and investigate the sensitivity of precipitation patterns to sea surface temperature (SST) changes. We find that the precipitation in our selected target region is mainly associated with monsoonal circulation and that fewer extratropical cyclones reach the target region from west than in the pre-industrial climate. Additionally, we find tropical cyclones in the model simulation, which reach the mid-latitude target region and contribute significantly to the summer precipitation. The co-existence of an extremely warm tropical ocean and the large-scale monsoonal circulation promotes tropical cyclones to reach the continental mid-latitudes, presenting an additional pathway for moisture transport into the mid-latitudes. Our sensitivity experiments show that the precipitation in our mid-latitude continental target area is sensitive to the land-sea temperature contrast, and that lowering SST values enhance the monsoonal circulation which then transports more moisture inland. Our study thus highlights that the early Eocene climate simulation underestimates the monsoonal circulation and precipitation across the continental interior of East Asia, which is likely connected to a discrepancy in the land sea thermal contrast.

papers.title: Deconvoluting the influence of environmental forcings on chemical weathering rates using machine learning model
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“青藏高原”：标题或摘要命中 tibetan plateau、plateau、climate、precipitation，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: Quantifying the contributions of silicate and carbonate weathering to global carbon dioxide sequestration is crucial for understanding Earth’s climate regulation mechanisms. In this study, we introduce a framework that integrates explainable machine learning with partial dependence analysis to understand the relationships between environmental forcings and chemical weathering rates. We trained machine learning models on a geochemical dataset from the Tibetan Plateau together with climatic and environmental factors, achieving a weathering model with high predictive ability (R 2 = 0.84–0.96). Furthermore, we separated direct environmental driving effects from indirect mediating effects through systemic partial dependence plots. The results indicate that runoff is the dominant controlling factor of both riverine dissolved SiO 2 and HCO 3 ⁻ flux. Warming promotes riverine HCO 3 ⁻ flux in the river, but its effect on riverine dissolved SiO 2 flux is bidirectional-first inhibiting, then promoting. Further, our analysis reveals that the effect of precipitation on riverine dissolved SiO 2 flux is mainly mediated indirectly by runoff. Our study establishes a framework for investigating chemical weathering, highlighting the potential of machine learning to advance predictive modeling and reveal complex interactions between environmental forcings and chemical weathering.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal Heterogeneity in Cascading Snow-Hydrological Responses to Warming and Wetting on the Tibetan Plateau
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“青藏高原”：标题或摘要命中 tibetan plateau、plateau、climate、precipitation、temperature，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: Abstract. Tibetan Plateau (TP) has experienced significant warming-wetting trends in recent years, inducing snowfall changes. However, the relative roles of precipitation and temperature in driving changes in snowfall and subsequent snow-hydrological processes remain poorly understood. We use China Meteorological Forcing Dataset (CMFD) v2.0 to quantify the contribution of meteorological factors including precipitation and air temperature to variations in snowfall. The results indicates that snowfall variability arises from complex interplay of both synergistic and competing effects between warming-wetting trends, with pronounced spatiotemporal and seasonal heterogeneity. Precipitation is the primary factor dominating snowfall variation during different stages, affecting snowfall changes across 66.42 % areas of the TP. The compensatory effect of precipitation change offsetting warming-induced snowfall decline has intensified, especially after 2000, with positive contribution of 15.28 mm. Besides, the contribution mechanisms governing snowfall changes show phased elevation dependence, with mid-to-high elevation regions exhibiting greater sensitivity. Furthermore, sensitivity analyses based on the SSiB3 (Simplified Simple Biosphere Model version 3) land surface model reveal that warming-wetting induces cascading impacts through the “warming-wetting-snowfall-snow cover-snowmelt runoff (SMR)” chain. This cascading process leads to an overall increase of 2.2 % in cumulative SMR, accompanied by enhanced spatial heterogeneity and seasonal variability of snowmelt. Distinct responses are observed among different snowfall-contribution regimes, snow regimes, and elevation bands. Changes in dominant climatic factors reshape the seasonal distribution of SMR. These findings reveal the complex mechanisms linking snowfall changes to cascading snow-hydrological responses under a warming-wetting climate over the TP, providing novel insights for water resource assessment and future climate adaptation.

papers.title: Mapping chronic environmental pressure in Goa using machine learning and deep learning
papers.journal: Asian Journal of Water Environment and Pollution
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“AI × 气候”：标题或摘要命中 machine learning、deep learning、atmospher，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: Coastal landscapes experience overlapping environmental pressures that require integrated spatial assessment. This study combines satellite and geospatial indicators to map chronic environmental pressure in Goa, India. Fifteen predictors represent atmospheric composition, terrain, land-surface conditions, land use, and human activity. Time-filtered products cover available observations within a nominal 2018–2023 period, alongside static and differently dated products. Of 89 expert-informed reference records, 81 supplied predictor information for three tree-based algorithms and four neural-network architectures. Their probabilities were combined into an environmental-pressure classification. Low-, moderate-, and high-classes accounted for 56.75%, 30.54%, and 12.71% of valid mapped pixels, respectively. Higher scores characterised urban and industrial corridors, whereas forested eastern areas generally recorded lower scores. Night-time lights had the largest contribution to the high-class extreme gradient boosting Shapley additive explanations. Model scores align with the expert-informed reference classes. The integrated maps provide a relative screening framework in selecting locations for further environmental observation.

papers.title: Enhanced Surface Coupling but Suppressed Convective Triggering During Humid–Hot Extremes in the Yangtze River Basin, a Major Humid‐Heat Hotspot in China
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“东亚气候”：标题或摘要命中 yangtze、precipitation、atmospher，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: Abstract Compound humid‐hot extremes bring growing threats to human society, yet land–atmosphere feedbacks regulating these events remain insufficiently understood. Using high‐resolution observational and reanalysis data, we reveal that the Yangtze River Basin (YRB) is a prominent hotspot for humid‐hot extremes, with rare hot‐only events. Comparing humid‐hot and non‐humid‐hot days, we find that humid‐hot extremes are sustained by positive feedbacks involving a high‐pressure anomaly, suppressed clouds and precipitation, drier soils, enhanced evapotranspiration, and lower relative humidity—mutually reinforcing the extreme state. Land–atmosphere coupling strengthens substantially for near‐surface variables, indicating stronger land surface control. Yet this enhanced coupling does not extend to cloud development: elevated lifting condensation levels and reduced relative humidity inhibit cloud formation, leading to a decoupling between convection and cloud development and allowing humid‐hot extremes to persist. Our findings highlight the role of land surface processes in modulating compound extremes and provide a foundation for improving their prediction.
